title: Runtime Asset Manifest
description:
What the game loads, written into the game repository at public/assets/assets.json by whatever produced the asset manifest. It is not an artifact: it carries no provenance and no timestamp, because it ships inside the build and must be byte-identical for identical assets. The asset manifest (the artifact) records its path and hash.

Every `url` is relative to the runtime manifest's own URL, so the same file works at a site root, under a portal's sub-path and from a zip. Keys are sorted and the file ends in a newline; nothing in it depends on the machine, the directory or the order a filesystem listed files in.

A game resolves an asset by id: `assets[id]` gives its type and either a `url` (its own file) or an `atlas` and `frame` (a frame of `atlases[atlas]`).

atlases.description: Texture atlases packed from atlas groups. Load the pair once; each member asset is a frame.

files.description: Every file a `url` or `data` names, with its size and sha256, for cache-busting and for checking that what shipped is what was built.

url.description: Relative to this manifest. Forward slashes, no scheme, no leading slash, never leaving public/.

scale.description: The resolution the pixels were authored at: a 2x asset has twice the pixels of its logical size. Display size = pixel size / scale.

width.description: Pixels of the file (or of the frame, for an atlas member).

placeholder.description: A stand-in; the final asset is still owed.

atlas.description: The atlas this asset is a frame of.

frames.description: A spritesheet's frame names, in natural order.

family.description: A font's CSS font-family: the asset id for a font file, or the fallback stack when no file is delivered.
